newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler, UAW reach tentative pact.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler, UAW reach tentative pact.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Wednesday it reached a tentative agreement to end a month-old strike at an engine plant here that has crippled production of some of its most profitable trucks and sport utility vehicles.
Details of the pact were not disclosed. Company officials said the deal was reached early Wednesday afternoon after marathon talks that started on Tuesday afternoon.
The strike, the most disruptive at the nation's third largest automaker in more than 20 years, already has cost Chrysler more than $300 million, industry analysts have said.
The 1,856 members of United Auto Workers union Local 51 who walked off the job shortly before midnight April 9 are expected to vote on the deal Friday, a Chrysler spokesman said.
Union officials earlier confirmed published reports that a broad understanding on a key issue in the strike, farming out work to outside sources, had been reached by senior negotiators.

UAW members have insisted Chrysler drop plans to shift production of drive shafts at the big Mound Road plant in Detroit to an outside supplier, a practice known as outsourcing, that they say would result in the loss of about 300 jobs.
The plant supplies most of the engines and rear-wheel drive components for Chrysler pickup trucks, Jeep Cherokees and Grand Cherokees, the Viper sports car, and other models.
The Detroit Free Press and Detroit News reported Wednesday that company and union officials reached a broad agreement on the outsourcing issue.

Meanwhile, talks aimed at resolving two strikes against General Motors Corp. continued Wednesday. Those strikes have forced GM to halt production of its Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass cars in Oklahoma City and some pickup trucks at a plant in Pontiac, Mich.
